OMV's (VIE:OMV) Strong Earnings Are Of Good Quality
sum: OMV Aktiengesellschaft (VIE:OMV) just reported healthy earnings but the stock price didn't move much. Our analysis suggests that investors might be missing some promising details.

Importantly, our data indicates that OMV's profit was reduced by €767m, due to unusual items, over the last year. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Assuming those unusual expenses don't come up again, we'd therefore expect OMV to produce a higher profit next year, all else being equal.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Unusual items (expenses) detracted from OMV's earnings over the last year, but we might see an improvement next year. Because of this, we think OMV's earnings potential is at least as good as it seems, and maybe even better! And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. If you want to do dive deeper into OMV, you'd also look into what risks it is currently facing. For example, we've discovered 1 warning sign that you should run your eye over to get a better picture of OMV.

Today we've zoomed in on a single data point to better understand the nature of OMV's profit. But there is always more to discover if you are capable of focussing your mind on minutiae. The Bet OMV Holders Made
sum: If you only glanced at OMV headlines over the past year, the story looked messy, with decarbonization bets on green hydrogen sitting alongside geopolitical setbacks in oil and gas. Holding OMV over the past year would have returned 65.7%, including dividends. If you had been weighing that decision back in early November 2025, what within the bullish and bearish cases on record might have justified taking that risk, and what still looked like a step into the dark?
The shares cost €48.22 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at OMV then had to choose between two very different but plausible futures for the group.

On the bullish side, one camp saw fair value at €62.5, a level that reflected what that view considered a justified price for stronger earnings power. That story leaned on OMV’s push into green hydrogen and chemicals, including early work on a large 140 megawatt electrolyzer.

The bearish narrative pointed to a fair value of €40, again simply the price implied by its own more cautious assumptions. This view stressed decarbonization policies eroding oil and gas demand and the risk that some hydrocarbon assets could eventually be written down.

The clearest new fact was OMV securing a €450 million European Investment Bank loan and moving into electrolyser installation for its 140 MW green hydrogen plant, directly backing the bullish argument that transition projects were real rather than aspirational. Quarterly data pointed the same way. Revenue reached €8,715 million and net income €1,024 million in Q3 2026, with net margin at 11.7%, so profitability improved versus Q3 2025. Taken together, this evidence supported the optimistic case more than the cautious one.

The lesson is simple. When a thesis hinges on decarbonization projects and better margins, do not stop at capex headlines. Track whether funded projects hit construction milestones and whether net margin, not just revenue, moves towards the scenario investors were underwriting.
OMV now trades at €72.9, after a 65.7% gain over the past year. The selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level, so it sees the current quote as already baking in a lot of good news.

OMV stock: Q3 clean CCS result jumps 68% on fuels strength
sum: OMV reported a stronger third quarter on October 29, with the integrated energy group benefiting from higher commodity prices and sharply improved refining margins. In its third-quarter results release, OMV said clean CCS operating result rose 68% from a year earlier to EUR 2,117 million. Clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders of the parent reached EUR 1,153 million, while clean CCS earnings per share nearly doubled to EUR 3.54.

Energy clean operating result increased 51% to EUR 936 million. OMV attributed the improvement mainly to higher realized oil and gas prices, which offset lower sales volumes caused in part by missing liftings in the Middle East amid regional logistics constraints. Hydrocarbon production declined 3% to 294 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day.

Fuels delivered the largest earnings contribution. Its clean CCS operating result climbed to EUR 1,124 million from EUR 413 million in the prior-year quarter. Higher European and Middle Eastern refining margins, strong refinery utilization and a more favorable product mix supported the increase. OMV's European refining indicator margin more than tripled to USD 37.50 per barrel.

Chemicals provided a counterweight. Its clean operating result fell to EUR 63 million from EUR 222 million as benchmark prices weakened and Borouge International contributed EUR 16 million. The figures are clean CCS or clean operating measures where stated and therefore exclude the relevant effects of special items and crude-price changes.

Operating cash flow rose to EUR 2,199 million, while cash flow excluding net working capital effects reached EUR 2,334 million. OMV ended the quarter with net debt of EUR 4,403 million and a leverage ratio of 17%, giving investors a balance-sheet reference as the group continues to fund capital spending and strategic projects.

items.t: OMV stock trades 2.65% below Monday morning quote
sum: OMV stock traded at 73.60 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:10 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 2.65 percent below the 75.60-euro quote cited in the morning report. The new quote was 0.20 percent below the Xetra close of 73.75 euros on Monday, November 2.
The move followed a morning report on BlackRock's voting position and comes against a stronger quarterly operating backdrop. Investors can use the real-time quote of OMV stock to follow the listing.

BlackRock reported that its total voting position in OMV crossed the 5 percent threshold on October 28. OMV released the holding announcement on October 29, and the filing was published by Deutsche Boerse.

The filing showed 4.53 percent of voting rights attached to shares and 0.47 percent through financial instruments. It compared with a 4.99 percent total position in the previous notification and covered 327,272,727 voting rights.
The disclosure records a regulatory ownership change, not a stated strategic role for BlackRock. It also does not indicate how the asset manager intends to vote.

In its third-quarter release dated October 29, OMV reported a clean CCS Operating Result of 2,117 million euros, up 68 percent from the prior-year quarter. Clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders reached 1,153 million euros, while operating cash flow stood at 2,199 million euros.

The results provide a stronger earnings base for the energy group, although the ownership notice alone does not change OMV's operating outlook. Investors will continue to weigh commodity prices, refining margins and project execution alongside shareholder disclosures.

OMV stock outlook: Petrom shareholders face higher capex vote
sum: OMV Petrom shareholders are due to meet on Friday, November 6, 2026, with a proposed increase in the Romanian group’s 2026 capital spending budget on the agenda. The proposal follows the company’s third-quarter report published on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The OMV Petrom quarterly report says the meeting is expected to consider an increase of about 1 billion Romanian leu in the 2026 CAPEX budget, taking it to about 10 billion Romanian leu. The report links the higher investment plan mainly to increased spending on the Neptun Deep project and also points to larger investments in low- and zero-carbon projects.

OMV Petrom reported a clean CCS operating result of 2.782 billion Romanian leu for the third quarter, up 103 percent from the year-earlier period. Clean CCS net income attributable to the parent’s shareholders increased 47 percent to 2.249 billion Romanian leu, while operating cash flow rose 67 percent to 3.651 billion Romanian leu.

The stronger operating performance came as higher commodity prices and refining margins supported the exploration and production as well as refining and marketing businesses. The company also reported a 100 percent refinery utilization rate for the quarter, compared with 96 percent a year earlier.

The November 6 vote is the immediate corporate event for investors following the strong quarterly figures. The report says first gas from Neptun Deep is expected in the first half of 2027, making execution of the development program a central medium-term issue.
OMV stock traded at 75.53 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:27 CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The real-time quote of OMV stock provides the latest trading view.

OMV stock: Q3 clean CCS result rises 68 percent
sum: OMV reported a stronger third quarter on Thursday, October 29, 2026, with higher energy prices and refining margins lifting earnings across its integrated energy business. In its third-quarter results release, OMV said its clean CCS Operating Result increased 68 percent year over year to 2,117 million euros. Clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders of the parent reached 1,153 million euros, up 94 percent, while clean CCS earnings per share rose 95 percent to 3.54 euros.

Sales revenues from continuing operations increased 43 percent to 8,959 million euros. Operating cash flow more than doubled to 2,199 million euros, and cash flow excluding net working capital effects rose 57 percent to 2,334 million euros. OMV said the stronger cash generation also reflected the first Borouge International dividend, while the balance sheet ended the quarter with net debt of 4,403 million euros and a leverage ratio of 17 percent.

The Energy segment's clean Operating Result rose 51 percent to 936 million euros. Higher realized oil and gas prices more than offset lower sales volumes, which OMV linked to logistical constraints and the lack of liftings in the Middle East. Hydrocarbon production was 294 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, down 3 percent from the prior-year quarter.

Fuels delivered the largest improvement. Its clean CCS Operating Result climbed 172 percent to 1,124 million euros as European and Middle Eastern refining margins, utilization rates and the product mix strengthened. OMV's European refining indicator margin more than tripled to 37.50 US dollars per barrel, while European refinery utilization reached 92 percent. Retail contributions were lower because fuel margins weakened after the rise in international oil product quotations.

Chemicals provided a counterweight, with its clean Operating Result falling 72 percent to 63 million euros. OMV cited lower market prices and a weaker contribution from Borouge International, although base chemicals benefited from stronger olefin margins and steam cracker utilization improved to 82 percent.
OMV now expects 2026 organic capital expenditure of around 3.5 billion euros, compared with its previous forecast of around 3.4 billion euros.

sum: OMV stock (ISIN AT0000743059) is responding to a strong third-quarter result, while the company also highlighted a sharp split between refining strength and weaker Chemicals earnings. The OMV release dated October 29, 2026 reported a clean CCS Operating Result of EUR 2,117 million and operating cash flow of EUR 2,199 million.

Operating cash flow increased 101 percent from the third quarter of 2025, while cash flow excluding net working capital effects rose 57 percent to EUR 2,334 million. Clean CCS earnings per share reached EUR 3.54, and clean CCS net income attributable to stockholders of the parent rose 94 percent to EUR 1,153 million, according to OMV.

The Fuels segment delivered a clean CCS Operating Result of EUR 1,124 million, up from EUR 413 million a year earlier. The European refining indicator margin reached USD 37.50 per barrel, compared with USD 11.50 in the prior-year quarter, while refinery utilization rose to 92 percent.

Chemicals provided the counterweight. Its clean Operating Result fell to EUR 63 million from EUR 222 million, even though steam cracker utilization improved to 82 percent. This leaves the quarter highly dependent on refining conditions and commodity prices.

OMV raised its 2026 organic capital expenditure outlook to EUR 3.5 billion from EUR 3.4 billion. It also expects Brent prices above USD 95 per barrel, average realized gas prices of EUR 45.00 per megawatt-hour and a European refining margin of USD 25.00 per barrel.

sum: OMV (ISIN AT0000743059) will publish its third-quarter results on October 29, 2026, a date stated in the company's October 9, 2026 trading update. The stock was trading at EUR 72.18 at Lang & Schwarz on October 27, 2026 at 4:47 p.m. CEST, down 2.33 percent versus the Xetra close of October 26, 2026 at EUR 73.90.

The scheduled report is the next major company date for investors. OMV said the update covered the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and warned that the provisional indicators could differ from the final quarterly report.

The operating mix already points to a divided quarter. According to onvista on October 9, 2026, hydrocarbon production rose to 294,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter from 291,000 in the second quarter, but sales fell to 225,000 from 242,000.

The year-on-year comparison was also mixed. Third-quarter production stood at 294,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day versus 304,000 a year earlier, while sales were 225,000 against 306,000. The realized crude oil price declined to USD 93.60 per barrel from USD 97.80 in the second quarter, whereas realized natural gas prices increased to EUR 49.20 per megawatt-hour from EUR 37.80.

Refining provided a counterweight in the same update. The European reference margin rose to USD 37.50 per barrel from USD 20.33, and refinery utilization increased to 92 percent from 90 percent. At the same time, onvista reported that special taxes could reduce unadjusted net income by EUR 150.00 million to EUR 200.00 million.

Boerse Global reported on October 23, 2026 that Jefferies raised its OMV target from EUR 68.00 to EUR 70.00 and retained its Hold rating. The EUR 70.00 target sits 3.02 percent below the Lang & Schwarz price.

OMV had a market capitalization of EUR 23.5 billion and a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 8.90 on October 27, 2026. Its 52-week range was EUR 45.68 to EUR 74.95, placing the current euro price 3.70 percent below the high. The next reporting date is October 29, 2026.

Hydrocarbon sales volumes fell to 225 thousand barrels per day from 306 thousand in the third quarter of 2025, a decline of 26.47 percent, according to onvista.

The same report said missed liftings could reduce the Energy segment's clean operating result by EUR 100.00 million in the third quarter. Special taxes were expected to reduce reported net income by EUR 150.00 million to EUR 200.00 million, while the clean operating result was unaffected by that item.

RBC's EUR 70.00 target is 5.79 percent below the Lang & Schwarz price. The valuation frame is less demanding than the target comparison suggests: OMV had a P/E ratio of 9.15 and a dividend yield of 6.00 percent as of October 23, 2026. Its market capitalization was EUR 24.1 billion.

OMV flags EUR 100 million Q3 headwind. OMV stock trades 9.60 percent above Barclays target
sum: OMV (ISIN AT0000743059) faces a EUR 100 million third-quarter headwind from delayed crude liftings, while Barclays set a EUR 68 price target for the stock. On October 9, 2026, Reuters reported that missing Middle East liftings were expected to weigh on OMV's clean operating result. Markets Insider reported on October 5, 2026 that Barclays raised its target from EUR 60 to EUR 68 while keeping an Underweight rating.

The third-quarter update presents a mixed operating picture. OMV's hydrocarbon production reached 294 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, down from 304 thousand a year earlier, while sales volumes fell to 225 thousand from 242 thousand in the previous quarter, according to OMV.

Refining provided the clearest counterweight. The European reference margin rose to USD 37.50 per barrel from USD 20.33 in the previous quarter, and refinery utilization increased to 92 percent from 90 percent. The chemicals division faced weaker conditions at Borouge International, while special taxes in Austria and Romania were expected to reduce reported net income by EUR 150 million to EUR 200 million.

On October 5, 2026, Barclays raised its price target from EUR 60 to EUR 68. On October 6, 2026, a Deutsche Boerse disclosure showed BlackRock's total position at 4.99 percent of OMV voting rights, down from 5.00 percent, according to Deutsche Boerse. On October 9, 2026, OMV published its third-quarter trading update with production of 294 kboe/d.

The key issue is the balance between stronger refining and weaker upstream and chemicals conditions. The EUR 100 million clean operating result headwind from liftings and the EUR 150 million to EUR 200 million special-item burden affect different profit measures, so the reported result may look weaker than the underlying operating result. The company also expects a higher contribution from ADNOC refining activities, which could soften the pressure.

OMV is scheduled to publish its third-quarter results on October 29, 2026, according to the company's October 9 trading update. That release should replace the provisional indicators with the full quarterly figures.
OMV's market capitalization was EUR 24.2 billion as of October 21, 2026, while its 52-week range was EUR 45.00 to EUR 74.95.

OMV and Energie Steiermark Join Forces in Deep Geothermal Energy
sum: - “Tiefenkraft”, a joint project by OMV and Energie Steiermark
- Successful seismic survey campaign lays the groundwork for the next project phase and an exploration well in 2026
- Significant contribution to the heat transition: potential of up to 670 GWh per year by 2037 – covering around 50% of district heating demand in the Graz region
- Next step: exploration well “Petersdorf 2” in St. Marein near Graz

OMV and Energie Steiermark are partnering to advance deep geothermal energy in Styria and actively drive forward the heat transition. At a joint event, the two companies presented “Tiefenkraft”, a joint project by OMV and Energie Steiermark, an initiative to assess the region’s geothermal potential. In the long term, this could deliver up to 670 GWh of geothermal energy annually by 2037, equivalent to around 50% of the district heating supply in the greater Graz area.

Between February and April 2026, a seismic survey was carried out along approximately 900 kilometers of roads used as measurement lines. The data is currently being evaluated and will form the basis for a detailed subsurface model as well as for the next project phases.

Berislav Gašo, OMV Executive Vice President Energy, said: “Harnessing geothermal energy is key to an independent and climate-neutral heat supply in Austria. With our expertise in geology, drilling technology, and project development, we are making a vital contribution to a joint assessment of the region’s geothermal potential with Energie Steiermark and helping lay the foundation for a sustainable heat supply.”
